meta.summary: For solidity physics classification, verify a concrete violation of object impenetrability before labeling a scene impossible; treat plausible physical behavior as the default unless clear evidence of objects passing through solid barriers is observed. / For solidity physics video classification, systematically observe objects and their trajectories to detect concrete violations of impenetrability (objects passing through solid surfaces or barriers) before labeling a scene as physically impossible; otherwise default to plausible. / For solidity physics video classification, identify objects and solid barriers, track trajectories across frames, and label a scene impossible only when a concret
principles: Require positive evidence of a specific physical violation (e.g., object passing through a solid surface) before predicting impossible; absence of clear violation favors plausible.
For the solidity category, focus narrowly on whether solid objects intersect or penetrate one another rather than on general oddities in motion, lighting, or occlusion.
Counteract impossible-label bias: unusual or ambiguous visuals are not themselves violations; distinguish rare-but-legal physics from truly impossible events.
Use fixed-camera stability to your advantage by tracking objects across occlusion, confirming reappearance is consistent with continuous solid trajectories.
When uncertain between plausible and impossible, weigh toward plausible unless a frame-level contradiction of solidity is identifiable and repeatable.
